facts.fact: Ooru Digital, the implementer, says e-Authentication services and digital signatures for São Tomé and Príncipe are in Phase 3 (2026) of a programme in active implementation with DGRN and INIC, to let citizens identify themselves online.

STP.note: SIGA is said to hold civil registration and identity records, but no link or exchange between the two is stated.
DGRN is named responsible for civil registration through SIGA, but no digital civil register for births or deaths is stated.

facts.fact: Ooru Digital, the implementer, says a national Data Exchange Layer is introduced in Phase 2 (2026) of a programme in active implementation by DGRN and INIC, to link ministries' systems.

STP.note: The 150+ services portal is described as delivered by Phase 1 and as expected outcomes; the page does not say a service is live or piloted.
No count or share of people holding a national ID is given.
No number given at birth is stated.
Nothing is stated about who operates, maintains or owns the ID system day to day.
No public register is said to be keyed on the ID number.

facts.fact: Ooru Digital, the implementer, says a MOSIP-based national digital identity system anchored in DGRN's SIGA registry is being implemented, with Phase 1 (2025-2026) delivering it.

STP.note: No other system is said to check people against the ID.
The 61% internet penetration is given without source or year or a statement that it is a share of people.
The 71% mobile phone penetration is given without source, year or age range, and may count subscriptions.
SIGA is called the national registry system, but is not said to be a register of the population.
No digital entry of births or deaths at local civil registration offices is stated.
Social protection is only listed as a service area and a Phase 3 sector; no social registry is named.
Taxation is only listed as a portal service area; no taxpayer register is named.
